- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- After sharp price spikes, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly — overreacts to volatility.
- Model shows persistent downward bias in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day forecast, suggesting mean reversion is not captured well.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 2–5 days, especially in downward trends — model reacts slower than market.
- Model underestimates low-price periods (e.g., 60–65 range) and overestimates high-price periods (e.g., 75–85 range) — exhibits asymmetric error.
- When true price drops sharply, model fails to adjust forecast downward quickly — exhibits lagged correction.
- Model often fails to capture short-term reversals — tends to hold onto previous trend direction longer than actual market behavior.
- Forecast mean is typically 3–5% higher than true outcome, especially in early horizon — suggests calibration bias toward higher prices.
